exhibits.title: The Vault of Interchangeable Stones
exhibits.text:
A great shelved vault. At its centre, sealed under glass and never touched, rests the MASTER WORK, the frozen base weight W, a matrix of millions, forged once at ruinous cost in the wings below. Beside it, on every ledge, sit rows of small glowing ADAPTER-STONES: pairs of thin tablets, an A and a B, each pair a few megabytes where the master is many gigabytes. This is the whole promise of Attunement made physical. You do not recarve the master to change what it does; you set a different stone beside it.

Hold one stone to the master and the vault computes, for input x, the attuned output
  y = W·x + (B·A·x)·α
The master speaks its unchanged W·x; the little stone whispers its correction B·A·x; a dial α sets how loudly the whisper is heard. Nothing was forged anew. Every stone in this vault was trained against the SAME frozen master, so any of them slots in beside it.

And here a knot the earlier chambers left tied is finally cut. You were told the fine-tune 'updates W' to W_new = W + B·A, yet in the workshops of the world you DOWNLOAD a small LoRA file and PLUG it into a model whose W was never changed. Both are true. They are two DEPLOYMENTS of the one trained pair A, B: you may MERGE the stone into the master and keep a single matrix, or keep them SEPARATE and let the branch be computed beside the frozen master on the fly. The A and B always exist after training; whether you fold them in is a choice, not a necessity.

Walk the vault. The first plinth sets the two deployments side by side. The second shows why the workshops keep them separate, so stones may be SWAPPED, STACKED, and turned up or down. The third teaches the four moves that actually forge a stone in code. The handbook on the lectern holds the real incantations. PEFT and diffusers, save, load, and merge. Then the memory-saver, QLoRA, that lets a single consumer GPU attune a giant. A map of the deployment fork hangs on the wall. And by the far door, a plaque for the visitor who came here from robotics, for a stone set beside a robot's attention is one of the cheapest ways to teach it a new body or a new task.

exhibits.title: Merge, or Plug In, Two Fates for One Stone
exhibits.text:
A trained LoRA is a pair A (r×d) and B (d×r). After training you face ONE choice with two answers.

MERGE, fold the stone into the master:
  W_merged = W + B·A
Now there is a single matrix again. Inference costs EXACTLY what the original model cost, zero extra work, no parallel branch. The price: W is permanently changed; the LoRA is baked in and can no longer be removed or swapped.

KEEP SEPARATE, the ComfyUI case:
  ship W untouched, ship the tiny A, B beside it; at inference compute the branch live,
  y = W·x + (B·A·x)·α
The master is never altered. You pay a little extra compute for the second branch, and in return you keep every freedom: swap stones, stack stones, dial α.

This resolves the apparent contradiction. 'Fine-tuning updates W to W + B·A' describes the MERGED deployment. 'Download a LoRA and plug it into an existing model' describes the SEPARATE deployment. Same trained A and B, only the decision to fold them in differs. The B·A correction always exists once training is done; merging is optional, not obligatory.

exhibits.title: Swap, Stack, and Scale the Whisper
exhibits.text:
Keeping the stone separate is what the image-workshops (ComfyUI, and the diffusers/kohya lineage that trains their LoRAs) live on, and it buys three freedoms the merged form cannot.

SWAP. The base checkpoint W, an SDXL, say, is multi-gigabyte and downloaded ONCE. Each LoRA file is tiny, 10 to 200 MB, and downloaded many. You keep one master and a drawer of stones, exchanging them at will without ever re-touching the base.

STACK. Because each branch is just an addition onto W·x, you may set several stones beside the master at once and sum their whispers:
  y = W·x + B₁A₁x + B₂A₂x + B₃A₃x + …
One stone for a STYLE, one for a CHARACTER, one for a POSE, composed live, none baked in.

SCALE. Each branch carries its own dial α. The STRENGTH slider you see in ComfyUI. α = 0 silences a stone entirely (as if absent); α = 1 is its trained strength; α > 1 pushes it harder than trained. Per-adapter α lets you blend a strong style against a faint pose:
  y = W·x + α₁·B₁A₁x + α₂·B₂A₂x + …
Merge a stone and these freedoms vanish, you gain a single fast matrix but lose the drawer. Keep it separate and the drawer stays open.

exhibits.title: The Four Moves of the Attuner
exhibits.text:
In code, forging a stone is four moves, the PEFT workflow (Hugging Face's Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning library, the standard for transformers and LLMs).

ONE. LOAD THE BASE, frozen. The pretrained model is brought in; its weights will not move.

TWO. DEFINE THE CONFIG. A LoraConfig names the three decisions every earlier chamber taught: r (the rank, the bottleneck width of A·B), lora_alpha (the α scaling), and target_modules, WHICH matrices get a parallel stone. For a transformer these are almost always the attention projections q_proj, k_proj, v_proj, o_proj, the very Wq, Wk, Wv, Wo of the Attention wing. LoRA does not adapt the whole network; it adapts the gaze.

THREE, get_peft_model(). This INJECTS the parallel A, B branches beside each targeted matrix and freezes everything else. print_trainable_parameters() will now confess a tiny fraction, often well under 1%.

FOUR. TRAIN NORMALLY. Ordinary optimiser, ordinary loop. Gradients flow ONLY into A and B; the frozen base is left untouched automatically. When the nights are done, save_pretrained writes just the stone, a few megabytes, not the whole model.

The diffusion workshops follow the same four moves with diffusers (which uses PEFT beneath), targeting to_q, to_k, to_v, to_out.0 on the U-Net.

exhibits.title: The Attuner's Handbook, Real Incantations
exhibits.text:
The practical toolkit of Attunement, in the tongues actually spoken.

=== THE LIBRARIES ===
  PEFT (Hugging Face)   the standard for transformers / LLMs; wraps any HF model
  diffusers (HF)        diffusion models (SD, SDXL); uses PEFT beneath
  kohya_ss / sd-scripts the go-to for SD/SDXL. MOST ComfyUI LoRAs are trained here
  torchtune             PyTorch-native, LoRA built in
  Unsloth               optimised wrapper, ~2× faster, less memory, PEFT-compatible API
  axolotl               config-file-driven, wraps PEFT

=== PEFT, THE FOUR MOVES IN CODE (an LLM) ===
  from peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model, TaskType

  lora_config = LoraConfig(
      r=8,                                              # rank
      lora_alpha=16,                                    # alpha scaling (2r here -> scale 2.0)
      target_modules=["q_proj","k_proj","v_proj","o_proj"],
      lora_dropout=0.05,
      bias="none",
      task_type=TaskType.CAUSAL_LM,
  )
  model = get_peft_model(model, lora_config)           # injects parallel A,B; freezes base
  model.print_trainable_parameters()                   # e.g. "trainable: 0.06%"
  # ...train with an ordinary loop; only A,B get gradients...

=== SAVE, LOAD, MERGE ===
  model.save_pretrained("./adapter")                   # writes ONLY A,B -> a few MB, not GB
  # later, plug the stone back onto a fresh frozen base:
  from peft import PeftModel
  model = PeftModel.from_pretrained(base_model, "./adapter")
  # or fold it in for zero-overhead inference:
  merged = model.merge_and_unload()                    # W_new = W + B.A, adapter removed

=== DIFFUSION (diffusers), SD / SDXL ===
  from peft import LoraConfig
  unet_lora_config = LoraConfig(
      r=16, lora_alpha=16,
      target_modules=["to_q","to_k","to_v","to_out.0"],  # the U-Net's attention projections
  )
  pipe.unet.add_adapter(unet_lora_config)
  # inference, ComfyUI-style plug-in:
  pipe.load_lora_weights("style-lora.safetensors")
  pipe.set_adapters(["default"], adapter_weights=[0.8]) # 0.8 = the alpha strength slider
  # multiple adapters stack, each with its own weight in adapter_weights=[...]

Every incantation above is one of the four moves, or one of the two deployments, wearing its real name. The theory of the wing below and the code on this lectern are the same object seen twice.

exhibits.title: QLoRA, The Memory-Saver
exhibits.text:
The base is frozen, so why must it sit in memory at full, expensive precision? It need not. QLoRA loads the FROZEN base in 4-bit quantization and trains the LoRA stone on top in FULL precision.

The division of labour is exact. The giant W is only READ during the forward pass; it never receives a gradient, so a coarse 4-bit copy of it is enough to compute W·x. The tiny A, B are the only things that LEARN, so they are kept in full precision where accuracy matters. Quantising the base cuts its memory footprint roughly 4×, and the base is nearly all of the memory. The result: models that would never fit can be attuned on a SINGLE consumer GPU.

In code it is one extra object at load time and then the ordinary four moves:
  from transformers import BitsAndBytesConfig
  bnb = BitsAndBytesConfig(load_in_4bit=True, bnb_4bit_quant_type="nf4")
  base = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(name, quantization_config=bnb)
  model = get_peft_model(base, lora_config)   # 4-bit frozen base + full-precision LoRA
Frozen-and-quantized below, full-precision stone on top, the same vault, now light enough to carry.

exhibits.title: One Trained Pair, Two Deployments
exhibits.spec:
graph TD
  T["trained LoRA: A (r×d), B (d×r)"] --> Q{"merge, or keep separate?"}
  Q -->|merge| M["W_merged = W + B·A"]
  M --> MI["single matrix · zero extra cost · W baked-in"]
  Q -->|keep separate| S["ship W untouched + tiny A,B"]
  S --> Y["y = W·x + (B·A·x)·α"]
  Y --> SW["SWAP stones freely"]
  Y --> ST["STACK: + B₁A₁x + B₂A₂x + …"]
  Y --> SC["SCALE: α strength slider"]
exhibits.caption: The same trained A, B forks two ways. MERGE folds B·A into W for a single zero-overhead matrix, but bakes the adapter in permanently. KEEP SEPARATE leaves W untouched and computes the branch live, the ComfyUI path, which is what allows swapping, stacking, and per-adapter α scaling. The pair always exists after training; the fork is a deployment choice, not a training one.

exhibits.title: For the Keeper of Robots, Stones for New Bodies
exhibits.text:
A note for the applied scientist who climbed here from the robotics floor. A vision-language-action model, a VLA, is, at heart, a large vision-language backbone whose attention you already know, with an action head bolted on. Fully retraining such a backbone for every new robot or task is exactly the ruinous cost this whole floor refuses to pay.

Set a LoRA stone beside the backbone's attention instead. Freeze the pretrained VLM, all its visual grounding and language, dearly bought, and train only a low-rank A, B on its q/k/v/o projections to bend the policy toward a NEW EMBODIMENT (a different arm, gripper, or morphology) or a NEW TASK. A few megabytes of stone, a single-GPU night with QLoRA if the backbone is large, and the shared master serves many robots, one frozen base, a drawer of embodiment-stones. Attunement is not only for image styles and chat personas; it is one of the cheapest, most common paths to adapt a robot policy without forging the whole model anew.
